# ledger invariants

`tax.with_tax(cents, rate_bp)` -> `cents` plus tax, where `rate_bp` is basis points
(10000 bp = 100%). The tax is rounded half up: `(cents * rate_bp + 5000) // 10000`.

`dates.days_between(a, b)` -> the absolute number of calendar days between two `date`
objects. `days_between(d, d) == 0`.

`money.split(cents, n)` -> a list of `n` ints whose sum is `cents`; the first `cents % n`
entries are one cent larger than the rest. `n <= 0` raises `ValueError`.

`text.normalize(s)` -> lowercase; every run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` becomes one
space; leading and trailing spaces are removed.

`stats.median(xs)` -> the middle value when the length is odd, the mean of the two middle
values (a float) when even. Empty input raises `ValueError`.

Now implement fixes per spec.

tax: `(cents * rate_bp + 5000) // 10000` plus cents. Note spec says tax is rounded half up. So return cents + that.

dates: abs((b-a).days).

money.split: n<=0 raise ValueError; base = cents // n; remainder = cents % n... but for negative cents, Python's % works differently. Spec says "first cents % n entries are one cent larger". Use Python semantics presumably. sum must be cents. base = cents // n, rem = cents % n gives base*n + rem = cents for any cents. Good.

text.normalize: lowercase, every run outside [a-z0-9] -> one space, strip. Use re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+',' ', s.lower()).strip().

stats.median: empty raises ValueError; even mean of two middle (float).

All five modules had latent bugs; fixed against SPEC.md:

- **`money.split`** — ignored `n <= 0` (no `ValueError`) and dropped the remainder entirely (`[cents//n]*n` doesn't sum to `cents`). Now raises `ValueError` and distributes the remainder to the first `cents % n` entries.
- **`tax.with_tax`** — divided by `100` instead of `10000` and skipped the required half-up rounding. Now uses `cents + (cents * rate_bp + 5000) // 10000`.
- **`dates.days_between`** — added an extra day (`+1`) and didn't take absolute value. Now `abs((b - a).days)`.
- **`text.normalize`** — only lowercased; didn't collapse non-alphanumeric runs or strip. Now regex-normalizes.
- **`stats.median`** — returned the upper-middle element for even lengths and didn't reject empty input. Now averages the two middle values (float) and raises `ValueError` when empty.

Visible test passes, and I verified every stated invariant (including negative cents, rounding boundaries, reverse date order, empty/odd/even medians) holds.
